label: A finding becomes a decision only through the report
rationale: Chapter 14 opens with valid bug bounty findings that triage teams set aside because the presentation made them hard to follow, and later shows a Synack reward doubled after patient-data context was added. The chapter's whole argument is that severity is argued, not computed.

label: Impact must be reconstructed in the client's context, not scored abstractly
rationale: 14.7 states that testers have limited knowledge of how clients value assets, uses the decommissioning-server RCE as the case where tester and client disagree, and 14.7.2 lists three reasons the author's practice often declines CVSS: no environmental context, scoring subjectivity, and interpretive complexity.

label: The report has three readers with three different questions
rationale: 14.2 splits the audience into top executives, security/technology executives, and technical teams, and 14.11 organizes the document as an inverse pyramid so each tier can stop reading where its question is answered.

label: The findings are a story, not a list
rationale: 14.6 argues the narrative lives in the executive summary and that a scan result read closely is a story about patch management and end-of-life systems, aligned to what the client asked to learn.

label: Business logic flaws are the class where impact can only be argued
rationale: Chapter 8 says scanners are extremely poor at detecting logic flaws and that the security implication depends on the business value of the application; its case studies are severities that no scoring vector can produce.

label: Report quality is a process, not a talent
rationale: 14.13 prescribes a template, a fixed font/style, a chosen English variant, and a QA pass that checks executive-summary/content alignment, chart/finding agreement, header/content agreement, PoC consistency, and affected-host accuracy.

label: WAF evasion is evidence about likelihood, not a trophy
rationale: 13.1 states WAFs are not context-aware and mostly pattern-matching, and 13.2 frames a bypass methodology. Whether a bypass exists is what decides "mitigated in practice" versus "live" in a report.

label: Enumeration output is interpreted, not memorized
rationale: 2.1 says the real skill is interpreting tool output and correlating sources, and that no collected data is unnecessary. This is what makes the report's affected-host list trustworthy.

label: LLM assistance in reporting needs an anonymization boundary
rationale: 14.12.1 notes findings contain PII, usernames, and passwords, requires anonymization before processing, and requires manual review because output may be inaccurate.

label: Payload catalogue for modern web attacks
rationale: Chapters 3-13 are a large, current-at-writing arsenal of injection, deserialization, HTML5, and WAF-bypass techniques.
